met_analysis:
The Low Pressure Area over Southeast Rajasthan & adjoining north Gujarat lies over southwest Rajasthan adjoining Kutch region and southeast Pakistan at 1730 hrs IST of today 14 September, 2026. The associated cyclonic circulation now extends upto 7.6 km above mean sea level tilting southwards with height.
The Monsoon trough at mean sea level now passes through centre of Low Pressure Area over southwest Rajasthan adjoining Kutch region and southeast Pakistan, Rajgarh, Damoh, Pendra Road, Rourkela & Digha and thence southeastwards to Northwest Bay of Bengal.
The trough now runs from cyclonic circulation associated with low pressure area over southwest Rajasthan adjoining Kutch region and southeast Pakistan to Jharkhandacross Madhya Pradesh, & north Chhattisgarh & extends upto 3.1 km above mean sea level.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over Northwest Bay of Bengal and adjoining north Odisha & West Bengal coasts between 1.5 & 5.8 km above mean sea level tilting southwestwards with height persists.
The trough from South interior Karnataka to Southwest Bay of Bengal across Tamil Nadu and extends upto 1.5 km above mean sea level persists.
The Western Disturbance as a trough in middle tropospheric westerlies with its axis at 5.8 km above mean sea level roughly along Long. 78°E to the north of Lat. 28°N persists.
